problem: Existing long-video QA and embodied memory benchmarks rely on multiple-choice or human-annotated QA, are solvable via keyframes or guessing, confound memory with exploration, and neglect low-level embodied skills (navigation/manipulation) that must act on recalled information.
motivation: Embodied agents must use long-term experience (days of images) but VLMs handle only a few hundred frames. A benchmark is needed that isolates memory from exploration, is automatically verifiable, procedurally extensible, and couples recall with acting.
key_idea: FindingDory: a Habitat/HSSD benchmark with a two-phase setup (oracle experience collection of pick-and-place videos, then memory-dependent navigation instructions from 60 PDDL templates in 11 categories) evaluated with hierarchical VLM goal-frame selection plus low-level navigation.
insight: Frozen long-context VLMs (GPT-4o 27.3%, Gemini-2.0-Flash 25.7% HL-SR) are far below the oracle (95.9%), especially on multi-goal, spatial-relation, and ordering tasks, and get no gains (often degrade) with more frames. Only fine-tuning on the benchmark's train split (Qwen SFT 52.4%) benefits from longer videos. Relaxed metrics (SC-SR vs DTG-SR) show VLMs recognise large receptacles but cannot localise precisely, and the HL-SR vs HL-SPL gap shows they cannot pick the nearest valid target. Hierarchical decomposition further collapses performance (LL-SR/SPL) due to goal-image distribution shift for ImageNav.
method: Two-phase design: scripted OracleAgent rearranges 2-11 objects (400-3500 frames, ends 3 m away from last interaction) to create the history; then the agent gets images/poses/actions and must follow a memory-dependent instruction, isolating memory from exploration

Task suite: 60 templates in 11 categories (spatial, temporal, multi-goal; object recall, interaction, conditional interaction, attributes, spatial relationship, room visitation, interaction order, time-based, duration, unordered/ordered revisitation); PDDL predicates/quantifiers enable procedural generation and automatic verification

Dataset: HSSD scenes (107 train / 30 val), 1,478 train / 100 val episodes, 79,213 train / 5,876 val tasks; GPT-4o-generated attribute descriptions with manual review; Hello Robot Stretch, 4 discrete nav actions

High-level baselines: Video LM agent (Gemini-2.0-Flash, GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-VL, Gemma-3, GLM-4.1V-Thinking) selecting goal frame indices from timestamped video; Textual Memory agent (chunk captions + LLM reasoning); SFT of Qwen2.5-VL-3B on ~82k tasks with 96 subsampled frames
Low-level navigation: OVRL-v2-style ViT+LSTM ImageNav policy (DDPPO, VC-1 encoder) or deterministic mapping + FMM planner to the selected frame's pose
Metrics: HL-SR/HL-SPL, LL-SR/LL-SPL, relaxed DTG-SR and SC-SR; oracle solvability upper bound via teleport
Cross-benchmark: co-train Video-R1 data with 40k FindingDory samples with DeepSeek-R1-distill-generated CoT; evaluate on VSI-Bench

setting.backbone: GPT-4o, Gemini-2.0-Flash (frozen); Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Gemma3-12B, GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking (frozen); Qwen2.5-VL-3B (SFT); ViT/VC-1+LSTM ImageNav policy (RL-trained) or FMM mapper
setting.training_data: FindingDory train split (~82k tasks, 1,478 episodes) for SFT; ImageNav policy trained on 1,166 HSSD episodes, 500M steps; zero-shot VLMs otherwise
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 640x480 + GPS/compass; interaction history video with timestamps overlaid
setting.action_space: high-level: goal frame index; low-level discrete MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 10° / STOP
setting.privileged: Experience-collection phase uses oracle agent with privileged sim info; mapping agent uses depth+pose from oracle trajectory; evaluation teleports to selected frame pose

results: All frozen VLMs score below 28% HL-SR overall (best GPT-4o 27.33, Gemini 25.73), and near zero on multi-goal tasks, versus a 95.92% oracle. Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B reaches 52.44 but still only ~20-30% on multi-goal; hierarchical LL-SPL falls to single digits. Co-training on FindingDory gives +1.7 (SFT) and +1.85 (GRPO) MCQ accuracy on VSI-Bench.
limitations: Low-level navigation controllers are a bottleneck (ImageNav distribution shift, poor SPL), confounding assessment of memory
Oracle 'magic grasp' pick-place is unnatural and distractors are less prominently viewed than interacted objects; tasks are navigation-only in the interaction phase
Frozen VLMs evaluated on subsampled frames (e.g. 96 for GPT-4o due to cost) and single-shot multi-goal prompts; synthetic-only environment
